Initially, Rome was a small kingdom ruled by a series of seven kings, with Romulus being the first. This monarchical period, which lasted from 753 BC to 509 BC, laid the foundation for the development of the Roman Republic.

During the reign of the kings, Rome expanded its territories through a series of conquests, including the defeat of the neighboring city of Alba Longa. The last king of Rome, Lucius Tarquinius Superbus, was overthrown in 509 BC, marking the end of the monarchical period and the beginning of the Roman Republic. This significant event was sparked by the tyrannical rule of Tarquinius and the desire for a more democratic system of government.

The Roman Republic, which lasted from 509 BC to 27 BC, was characterized by a system of governance in which power was held by the Senate and the Assemblies.
